name: shopping-hub
description: Cross-marketplace product aggregation and price comparison. Crawls AliExpress, Alibaba, DHgate, Banggood, Made-in-China, Geekbuying, Chinavasion and eBay, works out which listings are the same physical product, and publishes one item page per product showing every site's price, minimum order quantity and disclosed shipping - translated to English, with forwarding-agent links for the sites that will not ship to the US. Products are matched on five signals - perceptual image hash, normalised title, brand, manufacturer part number and extracted specs - rather than titles alone, which are close to useless on these sites. Comparison is done on landed cost (unit price x minimum order quantity + freight + duty), because the cheapest unit price often belongs to the most expensive order. A US retail baseline from eBay is included, so the tool can tell you when importing is not actually cheaper. Also included: reverse image search, bulk/BOM costing, break-even analysis, price and restock alerts, supplier trust scoring, category browsing and full-text search. TWO SETTINGS THAT MATTER: 1. Set SOURCEHUB_ADMIN_TOKEN below. The admin pages are disabled without it, by design - container traffic never looks like loopback to the app, so leaving it unset would otherwise expose an unauthenticated admin panel to your whole LAN. Sign in with the token as the password (any username). Browsing, search and crawling work either way. 2. Leave Extra Parameters set to --shm-size=1g. Docker's default 64MB /dev/shm makes Chromium crash on heavy pages, and it fails silently - the browser-rendered sites just return zero listings. Everything lives under the single /config mount: database, images, browser profile and the editable YAML config. Back that up and you have backed up the app. A slim image (allornothing/shopping-hub:slim, ~0.31GB vs ~1.17GB) is available if you don't need the six JavaScript-rendered adapters or the eBay/break-even baseline -- change the Repository field above to use it.

paths.name: Appdata
paths.description: Database, downloaded images, browser login profile and the editable YAML config all live here. Back this up.

variables.name: Admin Token
variables.description: REQUIRED to use the admin pages in a container. Any strong random string. Sign in with it as the password (any username). Leave blank and admin returns 403 - browsing and search still work.

variables.name: Mode
variables.description: serve = web UI plus scheduled crawling (recommended). web = UI only, no crawling. schedule = crawler only, no UI.

variables.name: TZ
variables.description: Timezone. The crawl schedule in config.yaml is interpreted in this zone.

variables.name: Translation Provider
variables.description: claude, deepl, google_free or none. Without translation, Chinese listings cannot be title-matched and mostly stay on their own product pages.

variables.name: Anthropic API Key
variables.description: Used when Translation Provider is set to claude. Translations are cached by content hash, so a repeat crawl costs nothing.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User ID. 99 (nobody) is the Unraid default and keeps appdata editable from the host.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group ID. 100 (users) is the Unraid default.

variables.name: eBay Client ID
variables.description: Free from developer.ebay.com. Without it eBay falls back to browser scraping, which works but is slower.

variables.name: Proxy
variables.description: Optional. One http://user:pass@host:port, or several comma-separated for round-robin. Strongly recommended for sustained crawling.

variables.name: CN Provider Key
variables.description: Optional API key for Taobao/Tmall/1688 data. Without it those three need a one-time browser login, which is awkward in a container.

variables.name: Trust Proxy Headers
variables.description: Set true ONLY if SWAG, Nginx Proxy Manager, Traefik or similar sits in front of this container. Searching for something uncrawled starts a background crawl, and that is rate limited per caller by source address -- behind a proxy every request looks like it came from the proxy, so one visitor's limit is shared by everyone. Turning this on reads X-Forwarded-For instead. Leave it false when the port is exposed directly: the header is otherwise whatever the client typed, and trusting it lets one caller bypass the limit entirely.
